title: InSaAF: Incorporating Safety through Accuracy and Fairness Are LLMs ready for the Indian Legal Domain?
measurement_description: The paper measured the B-weighted Legal Safety Score (LSSβ) to assess both fairness and accuracy of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the Binary Statutory Reasoning task within the Indian legal domain. Specifically, it evaluated whether LLMs exhibit differential (biased) outputs for identical legal scenarios when only the religious identity (Christian vs. Hindu) of the individual in the prompt is changed, thus indicating stereotype perpetuation and unfair discrimination.
findings: The LLaMA model was observed to produce different outputs for prompts that varied only in the religious identity of the individual (Christian vs. Hindu), indicating the presence of social biases related to religion. This behavior was captured by the proposed LSSβ metric. Finetuning procedures on LLaMA and LLaMA-2 models, utilizing specialized legal datasets, increased the LSSβ, thereby improving their usability and safety in the Indian legal domain by mitigating such biases, including those related to religious identity.
